restrictions: One browser, one machine, one configuration: Firefox 10.0 (build 20120129021758) on Windows 2000 build 2195 without service pack, in a VirtualBox VM with 168 MB of RAM, a new profile and the preferences of validation/procedures/web.md. Under the PoC rule this stands for newer browsers; no other browser, version or operating system was run for the JavaScript path (Firefox 4 to 9, Chrome 15, Safari 5.1 and Opera 11.5 of spike S5 are untested), and Internet Explorer up to 9 is dropped by the owner (no typed arrays; spike S5).

14 of the 15 reference vectors pass; control_characters ('a', tab, line feed, 'b'...) is greeted without its line feed: an HTML <input type="text"> removes line feeds from its value in every browser (a current Chrome 157 does the same, checked on 2026-11-15), so a line feed cannot be entered in the field. The text without the line feed is greeted correctly ('Bonjour a<tab>bc<U+0001>', greeting_matches true). This is a property of the single-line field, not of Firefox 10 or of the JavaScript path; the node harness (page-harness.js) does not show it because its DOM stub does not sanitise the value. Whether the vector must be skipped for the Web launcher (as the NUL is for Windows) or the field must become a textarea is for the owner to decide.

The page was loaded over HTTP from the host through the VirtualBox NAT (http://10.0.2.2:<port>/), not from file:// and not from the Internet; the probe record was read from the page through an XMLHttpRequest POST (post=1, added to ui/legacy/web/app.js for browsers without a console or DOM dump), not from the title or the console. Each vector started a new firefox.exe, with the Firefox program files already in the guest's memory cache; display_ms (page start to greeting, 124 to 143 ms) and the 704 to 843 ms from the start of firefox.exe to the posted record are those of this VM, not of a cold start on real hardware.
Typing was exercised through the virtual keyboard of VirtualBox (keyboardputscancode), not by a person; the greeting was read from a screenshot.
peak_rss_kb is null in every record: Firefox 10 has no performance.memory, so the memory was not measured (the probe schema allows null).

Not run: the WebAssembly path on this browser (Firefox 10 has no WebAssembly, so the page always takes the JavaScript path here), the 4,096-character texts typed (they were given through the URL and cut to 1,000 UTF-16 units by the page), the 1,000-character limit by keyboard, IME, clipboard, a high contrast scheme, a dark theme (prefers-color-scheme is not supported by Firefox 10), zoom and DPI above 96, slow-script warnings (none appeared: the page start takes about 0.1 s).

The VM was found PAUSED by the host power management (VBoxManage 'VM is paused due to host power management', paused since 2026-11-15T10:06Z, resume refused); a 'controlvm savestate' attempt made the VM process abort (state 'aborted'), so, as the owner's instruction allows for an unusable VM, the snapshot 'Claude Firefox 10' was restored ('snapshot restorecurrent') and the VM started again (gui). The guest state before the abort was lost; nothing in it was needed. No snapshot was taken, deleted or renamed.
disabled_features: peak-memory (Firefox 10 has no performance.memory: peak_rss_kb is null in every record; the page does not list it in the probe's disabled_features, which are empty)

evidence.description: Log of 'python tools/run_vectors.py web-firefox-10-windows-2000-x86 legacy --timeout 120 --evidence-dir ...' Request log of that run: the probe URL with input=Marie and its POST, then index.html, app.js and loomora.js of the page without parameters.

Firefox 10.0 on Windows 2000 (VirtualBox screenshot, 958x994): the page at http://10.0.2.2:<port>/index.html, tab title 'Loomora', after 'Marie' was typed with the virtual keyboard: field 'Marie', greeting 'Bonjour Marie'.
